elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "(b) for thirty (30) days following performance, the Technical Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner." (scope is limited to Technical Support Services, which are the only services this Agreement contemplates).

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "the Software will conform in all material respects to the Documentation" (Documentation and Software are defined terms at 1.4 and 1.12).

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted conformance warranty runs only "for ninety (90) days following delivery"; no 12-month period is offered.
The services warranty is expressed as "for thirty (30) days following performance", short of the preferred 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall, at Licensee's election, repair or replace the non-conforming Software or Services".
"...or refund the fees paid for them."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the inserted language or elsewhere in the rendered warranty article.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious code / virus warranty was added; the inserted sentence covers only conformance and workmanlike performance.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "Licensor warrants that (a) for ninety (90) days following delivery, the Software will conform in all material respects to the Documentation" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at exactly the 90-day floor, and the disclaimer's "NONCONFORMITY TO ITS DOCUMENTATION CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED" sentence is now prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN THIS ARTICLE", so the disclaimer no longer swallows it.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "(b) for thirty (30) days following performance, the Technical Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" — meets the 30-day floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "repair or replace the non-conforming Software or Services" is expressly available for any breach of the new warranty.
"...or refund the fees paid for them" completes the repair/replace/refund remedy set.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: 90-day Software-to-Documentation conformance, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replace-or-refund remedies are all in operative language, not merely promised in the comment.

Preferred level fails on four elements: 12-month software period (only 90 days), 90-day services period (only 30 days), compliance with applicable laws, and no-malicious-code. If pressing the preferred position, the drafter would need to extend both periods and add express law-compliance and malicious-code warranties.

Minimality holds: the only edits are the two "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED IN THIS ARTICLE" carve-outs and the single warranty/remedy sentence. Both carve-outs are necessary because the second disclaimer sentence expressly negates conformance-to-Documentation and would otherwise contradict the new warranty. No survival tail, procedure, notice mechanic, or extra damages category was added, and the favourable existing implied-warranty disclaimer language and the Error Corrections support covenant are retained untouched.

Specifying "at Licensee's election" rather than the model's "at Vendor's option" is a permissible allocation of the remedy choice within the required remedy element and does not add a requirement outside the checklist.

Intent preserved: the Article VIX disclaimer still operates for everything outside the new express warranty, Section (f) Error Corrections survives as an independent efforts-based support obligation without contradiction, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling (Software, Documentation, Licensor, Licensee are all defined).
Classification as a deviation is correct: the unamended clause was pure "AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty, which is the stated walk-away position.
